question.passageWithMarkers: The structure of glass is, frankly, a bit of a mess. Clear and perfect __(A) as__ it might appear to our eyes, down at the molecular level, glass looks more like a random ball-pit of atoms. The technical term for this mess depends on who you're asking: for some scientists it is an "amorphous solid," for others a "supercooled liquid." In theory it's both liquid and solid, though, given the way it behaves, in practice it's really the latter. In fact, at room temperature glass never __(B) behaves__ as a liquid, even an imperceptibly viscous one, even over long periods of time (__(C) despite__ it can "sweat" if you don't add enough lime to the mix). Those misshapen sheets of glass you sometimes see in old stained-glass windows, thicker at the bottom than the top, are generally not that way because the glass is slowly sinking over time. Unless the church has endured temperatures of more than 400˚C, the chances are they are uneven because that's the way they were blown and solidified in the __(D) first__ place. Flat glass was only developed in the nineteenth century and we had to wait until the middle of the twentieth century for truly flat, thin sheets of glass. The paradox is that, despite it being one of the very oldest __(E) human-made__ substances, scientists still struggle to comprehend why glass behaves the way it does. Glass seems to obey most molecular laws. As one glassmaker put it, glass is not a material; it's a state.

question.explanation: old stained-glass windows(낡은 스테인드글라스 창문) 내부에서 때때로 보게 되는 '변형된 유리판들(Those misshapen sheets of glass)'이 주어입니다. 'you sometimes see in old stained-glass windows, thicker at the bottom than the top'은 주어인 Those misshapen sheets of glass를 수식하는 수식어구에 불과합니다. 따라서 문장의 본동사가 와야 하는 수어 자리(are generally not...)에는 복수 주어(sheets)에 일치하는 복수 복합동사가 필요합니다. 절 내에 정동사(finite verb)가 반드시 하나 존재해야 함을 인지하고 준동사(being)를 정동사(are)로 고치기
